Policy changes within the ADHD framework have recently targeted the structural definitions of key clinical and administrative indicators to improve assessment workflows and cross-sectoral collaboration. These updates reflect a deliberate shift toward more precise diagnostic criteria and earlier intervention strategies.

A significant change involves [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]], which has been split into two distinct indicators. This policy adjustment was made to better reflect two separate elements of the assessment process, both of which are deemed essential for a comprehensive evaluation [^src1]. By dividing the indicator, the framework ensures that each critical component of the assessment receives dedicated focus.

Additionally, [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] has undergone a major redefinition. The indicator was expanded to encompass a broader scope of cross-sectoral collaboration. More notably, its classification was shifted from a treatment indicator to an assessment indicator. This specific policy change was implemented with the explicit goal of facilitating earlier contact and coordination with the primary healthcare sector during the diagnostic phase [^src1].

## Claims

**Source: ADHD_2024.pdf, Page 6**
* Indikator 2b er blevet delt i to indikatorer for at bedre afspejle to separate udredningselementer, som begge anses for vigtige i udredningen [^src1] (indikator-2b)
* Indikator 4 er blevet udvidet til at omfatte et bredere tværsektorielt samarbejde og ændret fra behandlingsindikator til udredningsindikator med henblik på tidlig kontakt til primær sektor [^src1] (indikator-4)
